stories.kicker: The Rabbit Hole · The Telescope World
stories.headline: The Night You See Saturn's Rings, You're Gone
stories.dek: Every observer tells the same origin story: the first time the rings resolve in the eyepiece as a real, three-dimensional thing hanging in black. It is a small, cheap, permanent hook — and it has just been complicated by a five-hundred-dollar robot that pulls nebulae out of a city sky.

stories.headline: The Tax-Free Rule That Changes in November, and Other Deltas
stories.dek: What actually moved in the travel world since the last weekend edition — read first through an ex-Singapore lens. One change matters more than the rest for a buy-once shopper: from 1 November, Japan flips how tax-free works.

stories.headline: The Country That Stopped Buying the Future
stories.dek: On Tuesday, China reported that marriages had fallen another seven and a half per cent. Somewhere in the same week, its one reliably-growing consumer category — anime badges, blind boxes, plush companions — was quietly resizing to four and a half trillion yuan. The two stories are the same story, and almost no one has said so.

stories.headline: A Mountain Moves, and So Does a New Government's Footing
stories.dek: A magnitude-7.4 quake — Colombia's strongest in decades — struck three days after a hard-right president took the oath. The rescue became a test of the state; then it became a diplomatic quarrel over whose rescuers were allowed in.

stories.headline: The Cash Arrives 9 September. The Date That Matters Is 30 August.
stories.dek: More than 2.4 million citizens will get S$400–600 from the enhanced cost-of-living payment. Whether it lands in the first wave comes down to one small piece of admin — and whether the Rally, a week earlier, turns one-offs into something structural.

stories.headline: The Floor Softens, the Ceiling Keeps Printing
stories.dek: HDB resale prices have now slipped for a second straight quarter — the first back-to-back fall in years — even as a thin band of prime, high-floor flats keeps setting million-dollar records. For an owner, the two facts are not a contradiction. They are a map of where to stand.

stories.headline: The Frontier Model That Finally Fits Your Graphics Card
stories.dek: A fortnight after posting a 2.4-trillion-parameter model behind a licence that reportedly locks out half the West, Alibaba shipped the version that matters to a home lab: Qwen3.8-27B, dense, multimodal, Apache-2.0 — and small enough to load on a single card.

stories.headline: The Best 360 Camera There Is — and the Question It Can't Answer
stories.dek: The Insta360 X6 shipped this week to near-unanimous reviews: bigger sensors, native 8K, and image quality that finally beats the GoPro Max 2. At US$699 it is a genuine buy-once tool. It is also the fourth "crown" in four years — which is the buy-once problem in miniature.

stories.headline: A 1990s Stereo, Reissued in Black, for the Price of a Car
stories.dek: Hiroshi Fujiwara's Fragment has reworked Bang & Olufsen's Beosystem 9000c — a modern take on David Lewis's 1990s CD icon — in black anodised aluminium, with a lightning-bolt on the clamper. It is sixty thousand euros of pure object, it began in Tokyo, and it is the week's clearest case of buying a feeling.

stories.headline: Six Years of Silence, Broken Quietly
stories.dek: Phoebe Bridgers released her first album since 2020 to the best reviews of her career — and a critic-versus-listener gap worth watching. At the multiplex, a dinosaur picture posted numbers no dinosaur picture has managed this century.

stories.headline: It Isn't the Phone. It's the Friend on the Other End.
stories.dek: A sleep-lab experiment on teenage girls found that socialising online pushed bedtime back by an average of nine minutes — a delay too small to be statistically significant, and concentrated entirely among girls with close friendships. The lesson for an eleven-year-old is about the pull, not the device.

stories.kicker: The Macro Desk · One Force, Four Instruments
stories.headline: A Record on the Board, and the Long Bond That Won't Applaud
stories.dek: Tame inflation set a record on the S&P and knocked back the odds of a September hike. But the thirty-year Treasury — the priciest it has been in a quarter-century — refused to join the party, and that is the tension the whole system now hangs on.

stories.headline: Can You Snack Your Way to a Better Engine?
stories.dek: The metric the longevity crowd treats as its north star is VO₂ max — and a run of 2026 trials says you can move it with brief, vigorous bursts you do on a stairwell between meetings. The promise is real; the fine print is who it works for.
